I can handle fractions, it's the arbitrary units relationships that get me. Like a mile. What's the significance of 5280? Or 1760? Or 3 or 12? Why can't we just use a simple logarithmic scale? Even if it weren't base 10, if there were just some consistency!

The mile came from Rome (as did the foot, based on Agrippa's actual foot) where it was 1,000 paces (where a pace was 2 steps). However, this measure varied from legion to legion (and probably day to day). After a few hundred years the British had a couple different measurements (miles were still based on 1000 paces, but they had the inch/foot (and nail, finger, stick, hand, yard, fathom, furlong from the Germans etc) that were all based on the size of a barleycorn 1/3 or 1/4th of a modern inch) and when their combinations of different measures needed to add up, there were some errors (a mile had to be 1000 paces, or 5000 feet, but also 8 furrow rows (furlongs) which were 10 gunter's chains that were 11 fathoms (2 yards) and the math didn't work out. So things were adjusted.

TL;DR: Most imperial measurements are based on body parts (so they're easy to use day-to-day in a rough sense) and were corrupted by the standards decay following Rome's fall, and the multiple conquests of England over the ensuing centuries meant that various measures were cobbled together not unlike the English language.
